Title: Make routing deterministic for a fixed question
Why: Six of fifty answers differed between two identical runs. Until this closes, no single-run pass rate is trustworthy to better than about ten points - including the 52/73.
Evidence: Pack re-capture 2026-09-22: indexes 12, 18, 22, 34, 45, 47 flipped

Building_agnostic: Cache key is the question, not the building.
Acceptance: The same question asked five times takes the same lane five times.
Notes: MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, and the row's premise needs correcting. Acceptance is 'the same question asked five times takes the same lane five times'. Baseline run of 10 questions x 5 asks, each in a FRESH chat (a shared chat lets the co-reference rewrite change the question's shape, CAVEAT-871): UNSTABLE 0 of 10 -- every question took exactly one route on all five asks. ROUTING WAS ALREADY DETERMINISTIC. The variance this row was opened about ('six of fifty answers differed between two identical runs') is therefore in GENERATION, not in routing, and a fix aimed at routing could not have addressed it. BUG-889 (the classifier cache keyed on the prompt hash, 0 hits in 38 calls, now keyed on the decision's real inputs) was worth doing but is a LATENCY fix, not a determinism one -- and W6-02 then found it left a 4.27 s RAG fetch sitting above the lookup, discarded on every hit (BUG-921). Re-run owed after today's changes to confirm 0 of 10 still holds. RE-RUN AFTER THE DAY'S CHANGES, 2026-09-29 evening: UNSTABLE 0 of 10 again -- every question took exactly one route on all five asks, so the acceptance holds and nothing shipped today destabilised it. Latency over the same 50 asks moved with BUG-921: median 21.0 -> 13.0 s, p95 79.4 -> 49.3 s (max 122.4 s, one outlier). Each question is asked five times, so four of five are intent-cache HITS -- which is exactly the shape BUG-921 made cheap, and is why the end-to-end median moved without any routing change. DONE on its acceptance, and the row's premise remains corrected: routing was already deterministic, so the run-to-run variance it was opened about lives in GENERATION and is not addressed by anything here.

Title: Latency
Why: Median 100 s, slowest 273 s. Acceptable for a demonstration, not for use.
Evidence: Pack timings 2026-09-22
Approach: Profile the register and metadata lanes first; forecasts are genuinely expensive and stay slow.
Building_agnostic: Generic.
Acceptance: Median under 30 s for non-forecast questions.
Notes: DONE 2026-09-29, and the row's PREMISE was wrong. Acceptance is 'median under 30 s for non-forecast questions': measured 4.46 s p50 over 48 requests (12 questions x 4 rounds, /chat, fresh session per question, BOTH caches flushed before every round), and 4.95 s p50 on a second run. The register and metadata lanes are NOT where the plan's assumed '100 s median' lives -- theirs is about 4 s. NO LATENCY REDUCTION WAS SHIPPED, and none is claimed: A-vs-B p50 moved 4.46 -> 4.95 s, far inside the per-question spread. What was shipped is the INSTRUMENT: `_safe_node` had recorded duration_ms into lane_outcomes since V12-19 and nothing published it, while `dialogue` and `response` -- the two largest stages -- were registered bare and not recorded at all. plan_trace.stage_ms now carries per-stage ms and /v1 emits ontosage_plan_trace, so the endpoint Open WebUI actually uses can be attributed for the first time. 97.8% of wall time is now accounted for: dialogue 43.1%, sparql 28.1%, capability 16.9%, response 9.8%. THE SPREAD IS THE REAL FINDING, not the median: identical questions with caches flushed ran 1.05 / 1.41 / 1.51 / 41.89 s. 47 of 48 requests had another turn finishing inside their window because the stack was in use; the variance is left UNATTRIBUTED rather than explained away (CAVEAT-500). UPDATE, LATER THE SAME DAY: one of the two reductions WAS then taken and measured. BUG-921 -- the classifier cache lookup sat below a GraphDB RAG fetch, a summarisation LLM call and an 18k-char prompt build, none of which its key depends on, so every hit paid full price for work it discarded. Moving the lookup to where its key is complete: dialogue stage on a hit 17,270 -> 119/132/157 ms on the very question this row measured at 9.5-10.6 s, and 7,503 -> 130 ms and 5,661 -> 201 ms on two others; wall 18.5 -> 0.6 s, 10.4 -> 3.2 s, 44.6 -> 13.3 s. Since this row attributes 43.1% of all time to `dialogue`, a repeated question is now effectively free at that stage. 157 ms cannot contain a 4.27 s fetch, so the win is structural and not an artefact of measuring on a quieter stack than the before-numbers. The trade is stated in the code and pinned by a test: `state.summary` is no longer refreshed on a cache hit. CAVEAT-922 (the register lane's two paths differ by 40x) remains deliberately not taken -- widening that vocabulary changes ANSWERS, which is not a latency row's change to make.

Approach: Seeded draw, hand-labelled, published with its denominator.

Notes: DRAWN, RE-RUN AND LABELLED, 2026-09-29. 62 held-out questions, zero overlap with the 51-question regression gate (normalised check against the gate's own output), so genuinely held out from what the system is tuned against. Re-asked AFTER the day's fixes -- the previous run predated them and would have measured the old system. Fresh chat per question and resp_cache flushed before each, because identical questions come back in 0.0 s having never run (lessons #149). RESULT, every answer hand-read: good or correct-decline 31/62 (50.0%); weird 14 (22.6%); FALSE DECLINE 7 (11.3%); weak-decline 10 (16.1%). UNACCEPTABLE = weird + false-decline = 21/62 = 33.9%. CONFIDENTLY WRONG WITH A FABRICATED FIGURE: NONE CONFIRMED -- the failures are declines and misreadings, not invented numbers, which is the distinction that matters for a deployment decision. Against CLAUDE.md's recorded 26.6% weird on tails K+L this is worse, and two things about that are said rather than explained away: this labelling counts a false denial as UNACCEPTABLE where earlier waves may not have, and tail M is a harder set of multi-clause stakeholder questions. 'Good' remains an UPPER BOUND until every one is traced to source data (lessons #121); the claims that were checkable were checked, and one (#34's 'on 1 floor') came back INCONCLUSIVE and is recorded as such rather than as wrong.
